stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +102.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $43.03 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 136 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 136 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-13.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-30) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: US basketball player arrested with 34kg of cannabis at Nigerian airport
stories.excerpt: The anti-drugs agency says the American attempted to leave the airport, abandoning his luggage with the drugs.
stories.lead:
A professional American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos.

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting to Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations.

stories.title: Flight disruptions expected to last into Monday
stories.excerpt: Congress recently gave the Department of Transportation $12.5 billion to upgrade the aging air traffic control system. President Trump wants more.
stories.lead:
Thousands of travelers are still waiting on airlines to reschedule cancelled flights after Friday's nationwide ground stop.

More than 2,300 flights have been cancelled and more than 8,000 flights within, into or out of the U.S. are delayed as of Sunday evening, according to FlightAware.com. Airports in Dallas-Fort Worth and Atlanta were experiencing the largest number of delays, with more than 250 flights each.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday that "by the end of today, end of tomorrow, I think we will be back to normal."

stories.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies age 80
stories.excerpt: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.
stories.lead:
Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80.

Félix Gallardo was widely considered one of the biggest drug smugglers in history and is credited with building an alliance between criminal groups in Colombia and his own Mexican cartel.

Known as The Godfather or the "Boss of Bosses", Félix Gallardo was the head of the all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel, which reigned over Mexican drug trafficking at the height of the cocaine boom of the 1980s.

stories.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
stories.excerpt: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
stories.lead:
NASA's Voyager 1 has traveled farther than anything else that humans have launched into space. On Wednesday, it's set to reach a new milestone: reaching a distance that is one-light day away from Earth.

NASA is celebrating the occasion with the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day." Calling it a symbolic celebration, NASA is asking the public on Tuesday night to send Voyager's call sign V-G-R into the sky in morse code. Use a flashlight, phone light or anything that can blink a sequence.

V - Three quick flashes, one long flashG - Two long flashes, one quick flashR - One quick flash, one long flash, one quick flash

stories.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
stories.excerpt: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.
stories.lead:
Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday as the US air-traffic control system continued to recover from a technical failure that led to a rare national ground stop.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said normal operations may not be restored until Monday.

"We have airplanes and crews that are out of position, so it takes a little bit of time," he told the BBC's US partner CBS. More than 8,800 flights were delayed and 2,400 cancelled on Sunday.
